reps.prompt: Use two documents together: explain how they corroborate (support) or complicate each other on the issue of government regulation of business. (Aug 2025 CLE.)
reps.station_focus: Drill corroboration: put two documents in conversation and explain what they jointly establish — the move is synthesis across sources, not summary of each.

stimulus.content: Frank Beard cartoon depicting the Standard Oil monopoly gripping smaller businesses.
stimulus.image_alt: Frank Beard cartoon depicting the Standard Oil monopoly gripping smaller businesses.
stimulus.citation: Source: Frank Beard, The Judge, July 19, 1884 (adapted)

stimulus.content: J. D. Rockefeller defending large combinations as opening opportunity.
stimulus.image_alt: J. D. Rockefeller defending large combinations as opening opportunity.
stimulus.citation: Source: J. D. Rockefeller, “Opportunity in America,” Cosmopolitan, September 1, 1907

reps.exemplar: Read together, these documents corroborate that trusts dominated the late-nineteenth-century economy — even as they clash on whether that was good. Frank Beard's 1884 cartoon (Doc 1a) shows the Standard Oil monopoly as an octopus strangling smaller businesses and banks, a hostile view of concentrated corporate power. Rockefeller himself (Doc 2), writing in 1907, does not deny that combinations had grown enormous; he defends them, arguing that large enterprises actually opened opportunity for ordinary Americans. The two sources disagree about value but agree on the central fact — that a few giant combinations controlled key industries — and that shared factual ground is exactly what made government regulation (antitrust laws, the Sherman Act) the era's defining debate. Corroboration here means using a critic and a defender together to establish the scale of the problem both were responding to.
reps.compare_focus: State what the two sources JOINTLY establish (even while disagreeing), then explain why that shared ground matters. Do not summarize each in isolation.
compare_checklist: Did I connect the two documents to a single shared point?
Did I explain what their agreement/disagreement reveals about the issue?
